items.title: A nonzero ideal in an algebraic extension of domains meets the subring nontrivially
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an inclusion of domains A contained in B inducing an algebraic extension of fraction fields, the lemma states that every nonzero ideal of B meets A nontrivially, hence that images of proper closed subsets of the spectrum of B are not dense (statement lines 6178-6184). The proof does not use integrality of B over A or a norm argument: it takes a nonzero element x of the ideal, converts its algebraicity into a polynomial relation with coefficients in A and a nonzero constant term, and observes that the constant term is divisible by x and therefore lies in the ideal (proof lines 6186-6192). The choice of the constant term as the witness is the step that carries the content. H2.
